subject: Priority: Dedicated pool throttling affecting FastCheckout - need ops bridge
messages:
From: Tim Greer <tim.greer@fastcheckout.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: support@fastcheckout.com
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Spike in 5xxs + latency on our reserved capacity - immediate help needed

Olga —

We're seeing a major surge in 5xx errors and median latency for inference calls routed to our reserved GPU pool starting around 08:30 PT. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to 3.7% and p95 latency jumped from 120ms to ~1.2s. This is impacting checkout flows for FastCheckout production (region: us-west). Our last deploy was earlier today and we haven't changed traffic weightings.

Attached is a short error sample and a snippet from our client logs that shows retries and backoff loops. Impact: conversion drop on several merchants, several calls timed out after 10s. Can you advise immediate mitigation?

We have an active SLA (Reserved capacity) and this needs urgent attention — our ops and CTO are on standby.

Attachments: fastcheckout-5xx-sample.log (text), client-retry-snippet.txt (text)

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Greer
Head of Platform
FastCheckout, Inc.
https://fastcheckout.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tim Greer <tim.greer@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs + latency on our reserved capacity - immediate help needed

Tim —

Thanks for the signal and the logs. Sorry for the disruption. I'm standing up an ops bridge now and looping in our Reserved Capacity lead (Marissa) and SRE (Sean). We'll triage immediately and get you an ETA for mitigation.

Immediate ask: can you confirm if the traffic is headed to the dedicated pool ID = dp-usw-7 (you can check in your integration config)? That will help us target the right pool.

I'm creating an internal incident and will follow up with the bridging details in the next 10–15 minutes.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0142
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Tim Greer <tim.greer@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs + latency on our reserved capacity - immediate help needed

Adding some context from telemetry — I pulled the last 6 hours from Grafana and there's a clear headroom collapse on dp-usw-7 starting ~08:25 PT. CPU/GPU scheduling shows repeated preemption and queuing. I have a snapshot link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/dedicated-pool-usage?from=now-6h (internal) — attaching a PNG export.

Suggested immediate mitigations:
- Emergency throttling on non-critical tenants routed to dp-usw-7 (we can throttle down a noisy multi-tenant workload that matches the pattern).
- Short-term migration of FastCheckout to a warm spare (dp-usw-9) for the next 2 hours while we stabilize.
- If migration is not acceptable, we can apply a temporary rate cap for specific high-cost routes for FastCheckout (you'd retain a degraded but working experience).

I'm happy to coordinate the migration (we'll need a brief window and a read-only test first).

Attachments: pool-usage-20260517.png

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs + latency on our reserved capacity - immediate help needed

Following up from SRE: initial analysis points to a single tenant exhibiting bursty, long-sequence traffic that exceeded our per-tenant queue controls and caused sustained KV-cache thrashing on dp-usw-7. We're seeing repeated requeuing and timeouts at the worker layer which cascades to 5xxs.

Immediate actions we took (10:00–10:04 PT):
- Activated emergency per-tenant throttles for suspected noisy tenants (reduced their token-per-minute to ~20% of baseline).
- Bounced a subset of worker pods to clear stuck KV state.
- Opened a drain for dp-usw-7 for new long-sequence connections while we validate migrations.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Migrate FastCheckout traffic to dp-usw-9 — we can do a phased shift starting at 10:20 PT, validate p95 and errors on a small percent, then flip.
2) Post-migration we will run a 1-hour soak and increase headroom for dp-usw-7.

I recommend we offer FastCheckout a one-week credit for the degradation while we root-cause the noisy tenant. That's an exec-level commercial ask; I've cc'd Vivek for visibility.

Attachments: telemetry-snapshot-grafana-link.txt (contains internal urls and query ids)

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tim Greer <tim.greer@fastcheckout.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs + latency on our reserved capacity - immediate help needed

Team —

Thank you for the rapid response and the suggested migration path. We appreciate the mitigation steps (we saw errors fall after your throttles) and would like to proceed with the phased migration to dp-usw-9. Please confirm the exact cutover window and a rollback plan.

Also — our CEO requested an exec-level update once we have a short RCA and timeline for permanent mitigation. Can Vivek or someone from your leadership join a 30-minute call tomorrow morning PT?

We'd also like to understand the commercial remediation you mentioned (credit) and next steps to prevent recurrence.

Regards,
Tim
